text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The interior ministry urges political parties to change their names and manifestos where necessary in line with new party law barring politicians from using Islam and Arab and Berber languages to rally grassroot support to win power.
- Soccer federation leaders fail to hold election meeting to end a stalemate in the country's main sport body.
- Security forces kill three "terrorists" holed up in a student dormitory in Algiers. The three men belonged to The Faithful of the Sermon, one of Algeria's small guerrilla factions.
- Sixty years ago, Algerian nationalists founded Algerian Popular Party to fight for the country's independence from French rule.
- The United States backs Algeria's legislative elections on June 5 and condemns "terrorism" in Algeria.
- The interior ministry warns political parties that April 21 is the deadline for registering candidates for the parliamentary elections.
